iconicAnchor.label: Madame Gres and Yves Saint Laurent silk drapery
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Fashion editorial traditions centered on fabric, silhouette, and movement
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Met describes pleated silk jersey, liquid silk crepe, chiffon, satin, and drapery as active determinants of silhouette, contrast, sensuality, and movement.

sources.title: Nan Kempner: American Chic - Evening Gowns
supports: Pleated jersey, liquid crepe, chiffon, satin, and velvet each create distinct drape, reflection, and silhouette behavior.
Fabric movement and technically refined construction support a tactile editorial sequence rather than generic soft-focus luxury.

sources.title: Fashion Photography: A Visual History
supports: Fashion pictures operate as editorial and advertising images that shape how couture and identity are understood.
The V&A's collection-based framing supports sequencing garment, model, and photographic treatment as one editorial system.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches silk, editorial pace, photographic, soft edge, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/silk-editorial/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
